title: BitemporalAssertionV1
description: Canonical bitemporal-assertion envelope (document 16 sections 3.2 and 3.4, shared foundation section 4.1). Both intervals are half-open [from, to) and non-empty. The semantic payload is immutable; recorded_until is the only field the ledger correction routine may close.

subject_ref.$comment: Identity or pinned-version subject, as the assertion type declares. A domain schema narrows this to exactly one form at its composition point.

value.$comment: Typed predicate value and the envelope's open payload point. Binary floats are rejected by the canonical hash engine; exact numbers use the released decimal-string rule. x-datacompany-hash-opaque declares explicitly that a domain which contributes no hash-view pointers here has its whole value subtree hashed as it arrives; the moment a domain declares any member of value, it must declare all of them. Arrays inside it still require their own ordered/set-like declaration.

valid_to.$comment: Half-open upper bound. An omitted valid_to means positive infinity; explicit null is not a released encoding for infinity.

supersedes_assertion_version_id.$comment: Corrected assertion version. A correction never overwrites the semantic payload.

recorded_at.$comment: Assigned by the authoritative service transaction clock, never accepted from a domain request body. Read-only in command schemas.

recorded_until.$comment: System-maintained ledger metadata, closed only by the correction routine in the same transaction that inserts the replacement. Excluded from the canonical hash view.

domain_extension.$comment: Declared composition point for the type-specific assertion payload.

command.$comment: Command form. recorded_at and recorded_until are read-only system time and are rejected on input.
